Title: Aligning Security Compliance and DevOps: A Longitudinal Study - ADS
## ADS. ## Aligning Security Compliance and DevOps: A Longitudinal Study. #### Abstract. Companies adopt agile methodologies and DevOps to facilitate efficient development and deployment of software-intensive products. This, in turn, introduces challenges in relation to security standard compliance traditionally following a more linear workflow. This is especially a challenge for the engineering of products and services associated with critical infrastructures. To support companies in their transition towards DevOps, this paper presents an adaptation of DevOps according to security regulations and standards. We report on our longitudinal study at Siemens AG, consisting of several individual sub-studies in the inception, validation, and initial adoption of our framework based on RefA as well as the implications for practice. RefA is a prescriptive model of a security compliant DevOps lifecycle based on the IEC 62443-4-1 standard. The overall framework is aimed at professionals, not only security experts, being able to use it on implementing DevOps processes while remaining compliant with security norms. We demonstrate how RefA facilitates the transfer of security compliance knowledge to product development teams. This knowledge transfer supports the agility aim of ensuring that cross-functional teams have all the skills needed to deliver the compliant products. :   10.48550/arXiv.2512.14453. :   Journal of Systems and Software, Volume 234, 2026, 112718, ISSN 0164-1212.

results.content:
Title: [Literature Review] Aligning Security Compliance and DevOps: A Longitudinal Study
## [Literature Review] Aligning Security Compliance and DevOps: A Longitudinal Study. # [Literature Review] Aligning Security Compliance and DevOps: A Longitudinal Study. AISolve security compliance conflicts in DevOps: This framework enables continuous, integrated security practices and assessment. This paper presents a longitudinal study on aligning security compliance with DevOps methodologies, particularly for products and services associated with critical infrastructures. The core problem addressed is the inherent conflict between traditional, linear security standard compliance processes and the agile, continuous workflows of DevOps. This challenge is especially pertinent for regulated industrial contexts, where adherence to standards like IEC 62443-4-1 is mandatory. The paper introduces a comprehensive framework designed to facilitate Continuous Security Compliance (CSC) by enabling product development teams to visualize, implement, and assess security practices within their DevOps processes. **RefA (Reference Architecture for security-compliant DevOps):** A prescriptive model that describes a security-compliant DevOps lifecycle. It maps security practices extracted from the IEC 62443-4-1 standard, along with other practices identified through literature and observation, to the eight widely adopted DevOps phases (Plan, Code, Build, Test, Release, Deploy, Operate, Monitor). **RefA-AP (RefA-based Assessment Protocol):** A utility guiding the execution of security compliance assessments for DevOps-based processes. **Problem Analysis (Studies 1-2):** Explored security challenges in agile/DevOps through Delphi and Lean Coffee workshops, identifying 15 challenges across five categories and framing long-term goals for secure development. This phase established the need to adapt secure development processes for DevOps and enable engineering teams to continuously assess and improve security, specifically targeting the IEC 62443-4-1 standard. **Solution Construction (Studies 3-7):** Iteratively built the framework based on design goals focused on demonstrating security practices in DevOps, enabling IEC 62443-4-1 compliance, and leveraging DevOps for risk-based decision-making. Key insights included the need for an artefact-based perspective (Study 4 after Study 3's activity-based limitations) and continuous refinement through trial assessments (Study 6) and expert feasibility reviews (Study 7). **Solution Evaluation (Studies 8-10):** Evaluated the framework against three research questions:. The framework is actively used by industrial partners to enhance existing reference models and elicit security capabilities for platform engineering systems. Future work includes extending RefA for risk management, cloud-native architecture security, and implications of collaboration structure changes on security practices.

Title: Aligning security compliance and DevOps: a longitudinal study - ScienceDirect
In recent years, an increasing number of IT/OT companies have adopted agile development and, in particularly, DevOps to build products for industrial and automation control systems (IACS) more quickly (Suzette and Yeman, 2023), to enable continuous adaptation and improvement of development processes (Hasselbring et al., 2019), and to support digitalization. However, the adoption of DevOps renders such compliance processes challenging since security standards come with process requirements that, while align well with structured (plan-driven) software process models, are difficult to reconcile with agile development and DevOps methodologies (Beck et al., 2001b, Standardization, 2022, Kim et al., 2016). Our work on Continuous Security Compliance (CSC) (Angermeir et al., 2024) demonstrates the limited discussion on agile development and DevOps concerning security compliance in literature (Moyón et al., 2020a, Bitra and Achanta, 2021). Furthermore, our previous work highlights that emerging approaches to security compliance require a focus on security standards applicable to product development and further validation in industrial contexts to demonstrate their feasibility and potential for adoption (see i.e. Our framework supports the reproducible and transparent adoption of normative security processes improvement in DevOps. Note, that the dimension of the herein reported longitudinal research program does not allow for extensive study methods descriptions. Since adherence to security norms, i.e., *security compliance* (SC), is a significant aim for product development (Fitzgerald et al., 2013), the present work focuses on SC of product development processes following DevOps. The third phase was the final pre-release evaluation of RefA, RefA-AP, and RefA-MR by an expert in the field of secure development of industrial products (Study 10). We have presented the development and evaluation of a framework that enables the assessment of security compliance in DevOps processes. In this paper, we present a problem-driven longitudinal research program entailing a series of empirical studies (see Fig. 1), involving 102 practitioners who have participated in the development process of twenty-six industry software products, twelve of which are related to our industrial context. These studies enabled the identification of relevant challenges and needs in the field of security compliance (SC) within agile development and DevOps. We framed the requirements and evaluation.

results.title: Aligning Security Compliance and DevOps: A Longitudinal Study
results.content:
Title: Aligning Security Compliance and DevOps: A Longitudinal Study
Our framework includes an artefact-centric model, the Reference Architecture for security-compliant DevOps (‘RefA ’), as well as, two utilities: the RefA-based Assessment Protocol (RefA-AP) and RefA-based Assessment Reports (RefA-AR) to enable the practical application of our model in security process assessments. Motivated by the problem analysis (see Section 2.1), we designed our solution approach as a framework for product engineering teams, where they can visualize and assess the security status of their agile development and DevOps processes in alignment with security standards. Finally, we interviewed experts to validate the suitability of RefA, RefA-AP, and RefA-AR for security compliance assessment of DevOps projects (Study 7). Can the RefA-based Assessment Protocol (RefA-AP) be used to effectively assess security compliance of software development projects following DevOps workflows? As part of a broader assessment of CSE practices initiated by product development stakeholders, we collaborated with several agile and DevOps transformation experts within the company to evaluate RefA and RefA-AP with respect to their security compliance. Once the assessment was concluded, we presented the outcomes using RefA-based assessment reports within the context of the overarching continuous software engineering assessment process to business owners, product development teams, the responsible security team, and other stakeholders. The specific goals of this study were: (A) determine RefA ’s accuracy in representing security compliance practices and artefacts, (B) determine subjects perception about RefA, and (C) explore the applicability of RefA-AP and RefA-AR for security compliance assessment in DevOps contexts. With the application of RefA-based assessment utilities, RefA-AP and RefA-MR, we learned that security compliance assessments: (i) can be performed more frequently than regular yearly/quarterly approaches, (ii) can fit within a two-week iterations, (iii) can produce incremental results either per DevOps phase or RefA practice area and (iv) can be performed by DevOps team members with limited support from security experts, if they have the necessary tools. These studies enabled the identification of relevant challenges and needs in the field of security compliance (SC) within agile development and DevOps. We framed the requirements and evaluation stage of our framework to enable SC assessments of DevOps processes, resulting in the reference architecture for security-compliant DevOps RefA and the related assessments utilities RefA-AP and RefA-AR.
